Beena Devi & Ors vs The State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 18
January, 2023
Author: Yogesh Khanna

Bench: Yogesh Khanna
 $~65
 * In The High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi

 Beena Devi & Ors.

entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Through: Mr.T.Kanniappan, Advoc
 petitioners.

versus
 The State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr. 
 Through: Mr.Sunil Kumar Gautam,
 State with Si B K 
 Vihar.

Mr.Puneet Singhal,
 withR2/complainant
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Yogesh Khanna
 Order

1. Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.50/2022 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Aman Vihar against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the son of petitioners No.1-2 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 03.12.2017 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
On 12.01.2022 at the instance of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.

The petitioner No.2 is an owner of the property No.100, Part-5, Block-A, Karan Vihar, Kirari, Suleman Nagar,
Delhi - 110086 and is residing at ground floor thereof.
The respondent No.2 along with her husband were residing at second floor of said premises.

The parties have amicably settled the matter as per settlement agreement dated 06.12.2022 arrived at before the Mediation Centre, Rohini Courts,
Delhi.

It is stated pursuant to settlement, the respondent No.2 and her husband have since vacated the second floor of the premises and petitioners have agreed to pay Rs.4.75 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims.

3. Out of said sum, the petitioner No.1 has already paid Rs.2.50 Lacs to respondent No.2 and for the balance amount, the petitioner No.1 has handed over draft No.002674 dated 04.01.2023 drawn on Bandhan Bank for Rs.2.25 Lacs in favour of respondent No.2, which has been accepted by her.

1 4.

entities.text: Beena Devi & Ors vs The State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners and left with no claim whatsoever against the petitioners and she has shifted from the property of petitioners No.1 & 2 with all her belongings and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
After receipt of settled amount, the respondent No.2 or her husband shall have no claim over the property of the petitioner No.1.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
6. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.50/2022 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Aman Vihar and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
